title: STILL PRESENT (r3): wrong-person awaiting transition still executes the unguarded update_reference_call_status — the taken_over_at backstop is dead code and the race pin is vacuous
evidence:
form_handler.gleam:1235-1261: `case row.taken_over_at != "" {
        True -> wisp.redirect(to: "/reference/" <> token)
        False ->
          ...
              case
                sql.update_reference_call_status(
                  config.db,
                  id_uuid,
                  sql.AwaitingCorrection,
                  "",
                  "contact_invalid",
                  sql.ContactInitiated,
                )`
update_reference_call_status.sql:23-24: `WHERE id = $1
  AND status = $5::reference_call_status` (no taken_over_at clause)
mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person.sql:14-16: `WHERE id = $1
  AND status = 'contact_initiated'::reference_call_status
  AND taken_over_at IS NULL` — called ONLY from the test at 1746/1758 (rc_sql.mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person(db, call)), never by the handler; the existing POST-route test (wp-taken-token, sequential take-over-then-POST) only exercises the read-time redirect and cannot catch the race.
detail: The mandate's backstop file exists but is never wired into apply_wrong_person; the executed UPDATE still matches a taken-over row (status unchanged by take-over) and yanks it into awaiting_correction. The pin calls the guarded SQL directly — vacuous.
recommended_fix: In apply_wrong_person's awaiting arm call mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person (0 rows → stand-down redirect); add a POST-route race test that neutralizes the backstop and goes red.
